title: Leek and Potato Soup
subtitle: Silky blended British classic
excerpt: A simple, silky soup of leeks and potato blended until smooth. One of the most satisfying winter soups in British cooking, made from three ingredients and transformed by the quality of a good butter and a proper blend.

recipe.sourceNotes: Leek and potato soup is one of the great simple soups of British cooking and shares heritage with vichyssoise, the cold American version created by French chef Louis Diat at the Ritz-Carlton in New York in 1917, who based it on a leek and potato dish his mother made in France. The hot British version is older: leeks and potatoes together in a broth or soup are documented in British cookery writing from the eighteenth century. Leeks are one of the defining vegetables of Welsh cuisine, and the combination with potato reflects both Welsh and Scottish food traditions.

content.text: The leeks must be cooked very gently in butter before any liquid is added: 15 minutes over the lowest heat until they are completely soft and sweet. This step is what separates a silky, flavourful soup from a watery one. Do not rush it. Blend thoroughly: a well-blended leek and potato soup should be completely smooth and pour in a slow ribbon from a ladle.

items.preparation: white and light green parts, washed and sliced

content.text: Melt the butter in a large pan over the lowest heat. Add the onion and leeks with a pinch of salt. Cover and cook for 15 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until completely soft but not coloured.
Add the garlic and cook for 2 minutes. Add the potato and stock. Bring to a simmer and cook for 20 minutes until the potato is completely tender.
Blend until completely smooth. Add the cream if using. Return to the pan and reheat gently. Taste and season. If the soup is too thick, add a splash more stock.
Serve in warm bowls with crusty bread. A swirl of cream and a few snipped chives on top are the traditional garnish.
